title: Rational Hom groups from integral models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Work with Noetherian separated schemes of finite type over $k$, the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. For such a scheme $T$, use the coefficient sheaves $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $E_T$ pulled back from the corresponding condensed topological rings, and let $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)$ be the full bounded constructible subcategory of $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda_T)$ for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E$. In particular the integral category is the derived-complete constructible category, as identified by [sk-lem-integral-models]. Put $K_0[1/\ell]=E_T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}K_0$.

Every object of $\Dbc(T,E)$ is isomorphic to $K_0[1/\ell]$ for some $K_0\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. For $K_0,L_0\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, the natural $E$-linear map
$$
\Hom_{\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)}(K_0,L_0[q])\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\longrightarrow
\Hom_{\Dbc(T,E)}(K_0[1/\ell],L_0[1/\ell][q]),\qquad h\otimes e\longmapsto e\,h[1/\ell],
$$
is an isomorphism. Moreover, if $f:X\to Y$ is a separated finite-type $k$-morphism between schemes of this setting, $K_0\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and $M_0\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$
f_E^*(K_0[1/\ell])\simeq(f_{\mathcal O_E}^*K_0)[1/\ell]\quad\text{in }\Dbc(X,E),
$$
$$
Rf_{!,E}(M_0[1/\ell])\simeq(Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}M_0)[1/\ell]\quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y,E),
$$
where $Rf_!$ is the ambient compactification composite $R\bar f_*j_!$, restricted to the indicated constructible categories.

proof.text: For the exact published boundedConstructibleExtendScalars F, use its existing localization instance at ell-power-torsion cones. Compare F to the Verdier rationalization Q with Localization.uniq and its comparison isomorphism. The scalar-fraction and equality criteria for Q identify its Hom map as localization of integer modules. Transport this along the fully faithful equivalence and its object comparison isomorphisms; full-subcategory inclusions identify these Hom groups with the ambient Hom groups.

proof.text: Check that the actual constant-section scalar actions in the statement make F O_E-linear. Restriction of continuous module sheaves is linear sectionwise. Exact restriction remains linear on derived categories by localization of complexes. The published coefficient-encoding square, derived through its composition isomorphisms, transports this linearity to internal module objects; the derived scalar adjunction gives linearity of extension. Restrict the integer-module Hom localization to O_E. Since E is O_E with ell inverted, IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange gives the E-linear tensor equivalence and its pure-tensor formula. Apply it to K and L[q], using stability of bounded constructibility under shifts, and postcompose with the canonical commShiftIso.

proof.text: Apply the proved continuousConstructible_integral_model theorem to the rational bounded-constructible object, using the induced norm and normed-algebra structure on the embedded finite field E. Its continuous valuation ring and coefficient inclusion are definitionally the published O_E and padic-integers inclusion, and its integralScalarExtension is the exact ambient derived extension in the statement. The resulting integral bounded-constructible object and isomorphism supply the model clause.

proof.text: For pullback, apply the published preservation theorem to each coefficient ring and use preservation by scalar extension. The published derivedPullIso is an isomorphism, so its inverse remains invertible after restriction. For lower shriek, use the standing compactification and apply preservation by open extension by zero followed by preservation under proper derived pushforward, for each coefficient ring.

proof.text: For the isomorphism clause of lower shriek, extension by zero sends the integral input to an integral bounded-constructible complex on the chosen compactification. The already proved continuous integral push comparison is invertible on this input for the proper, hence qcqs, compactification map. Its scalar inclusion is definitionally the published padic-integers inclusion for the induced norm on E. Expand the canonical derivedLowerShriekHom: its components are this push comparison, the open extension-by-zero comparison isomorphism, and associators. Each component is invertible at the input; pointwise invertibility gives the asserted restricted natural-transformation isomorphism.
